cards.objective: Name the pituitary hormone that controls the thyroid.
cards.front: Which pituitary hormone stimulates the thyroid gland?

why.t: Thyroid hormone release is controlled by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) from the pituitary, by negative feedback. Triiodothyronine (T₃) and thyroxine (T₄) raise the basal metabolic rate, the energy the body uses at rest.

simpler.t: Your thyroid is a small gland in your neck. Its hormones control how fast your body uses energy.

depth.t: Isthmus: the narrow middle part that joins the two lobes.
Lobes: wing-shaped right and left lobes either side of the isthmus.
Follicles: hollow spheres of follicle cells filled with colloid, where the hormones are made.
Parafollicular (C) cells: cells between the follicles that make calcitonin.

clinical.t: Too little iodine in the diet stops T₃ and T₄ being made, so TSH rises. The overstimulated follicles fill with colloid, and the gland swells into a goitre.

trap.t: The hypothalamus makes thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH); the anterior pituitary makes TSH.
